common_name: Crimson Pirate Daylily (Classic Red Spider-Form Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this classic 1951 Sass introduction is a diploid spider-form type that increases readily into dependable clumps.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Crimson Pirate bears star-shaped, spider-form flowers of fiery crimson-red flushed with gold around the throat and stamens, blooming over a long season from early into late summer. Introduced by Sass in 1951 and awarded an AHS Honorable Mention in 1955, it remains one of the enduring early spider-form daylilies still widely grown today. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Cherry Cheeks Daylily (Rose-Pink Trumpet with Golden Throat)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; this tetraploid 1968 Peck introduction has remained a popular garden variety for decades.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Cherry Cheeks bears large, rose-pink trumpet flowers up to six inches across with pale pink midribs and a golden-orange throat and matching stamens. Registered by Peck in 1968, this tetraploid daylily blooms in the late midseason and has been a dependable, widely sold garden variety for decades. Divide crowded clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor.

common_name: Jane Trimmer Daylily (Lavender Eyed Rebloomer with Picotee Edge)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid Trimmer introduction (Gillian x Sabine Baur) carries evergreen foliage and reblooms reliably with consistent moisture.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Jane Trimmer bears five-inch pale lavender flowers with a large purple eye so dark it appears nearly black, ringed by a matching picotee edge. This tetraploid Trimmer introduction (Gillian x Sabine Baur) carries evergreen foliage, blooms early midseason with good rebloom, and won the AHS Don C. Stevens Award for best eyed cultivar in 2009. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid Petit introduction from the year 2000 rewards generous spacing with large blooms.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Cleopatra's Jewel is a large-flowered tetraploid introduced by hybridizer Ted Petit in 2000, part of his daylily breeding program known for oversized blooms. Flower color and saturation can vary noticeably with weather, appearing softer on hot days and more richly colored in cooler conditions. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom size.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid Hanson introduction (Celestial Virgins x Prometheus Revisited), registered in 2017, carries semi-evergreen foliage.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Electric Ladyland bears six-inch, fancy edged rose-red flowers with a lighter watermark pattern, carried on tall, well-branched scapes. This tetraploid Hanson introduction (Celestial Virgins x Prometheus Revisited), registered in 2017, carries semi-evergreen foliage and blooms in midseason. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Ocean Rain Daylily (Orchid-Pink Blend, Hanson's First Introduction)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid Hanson introduction (Kings Throne x Enchanted Empress) was his first registered daylily, from 1987.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Ocean Rain bears wide-open, six-inch orchid-pink blend flowers with a glowing yellow-to-green throat, carried on scapes about two feet tall. Introduced in 1987 by hybridizer Curt Hanson (Kings Throne x Enchanted Empress) as his first registered daylily, this tetraploid with semi-evergreen foliage blooms in the early midseason. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.
